text:
alex: Quick sync on private deploy upgrade lanes. I propose we formalize 2 lanes: `maintenance-friendly` (avoid external IP renumbering, smaller risk, limited zero-downtime guarantees) and `swap-zero-downtime` (internal listener swap, external IP may change). Need field constraints and acceptance criteria.

sanjay: +1. From reliability side, `maintenance-friendly` should guarantee session continuity for stateful caches where possible. Main concern is KV cache invalidation during controller restarts.

mike: bundle note 1: airgap installer currently ~1.1GB. Field asks for <350MB. Spike options: compress assets, drop optional drivers, split optional-plugin bundle. Timebox 1 week.

lisa: launch checklist draft:
- operator runbook + rollback playbook
- preflight network checks (egress/ingress rules, iptables)
- KMS/HSM verification steps
- automated smoke tests against 3 representative netops environments
- telemetry + opt-out instructions
- support runbook for dual-listen troubleshooting

customer-noc: We will not approve any upgrade that changes our public IP mapping without 30-day notice. If you can implement `maintenance-friendly` lane that preserves external IPs, we can sign test approvals.

alex: OK we add a `--maintenance-friendly` flag. Document caveats: might need short leader-election pause (~30-90s) and requires nodes not be behind NAT that rewrites source IPs.

sanjay: testing: need a harness that simulates KV cache, long-lived sockets, and BGP/prefix stability. Failure mode we saw: after in-place upgrades some clients re-establish with new TCP source port mapping, breaking session affinity.

mike: sample CLI for field dry-run:
```
installer install --lane=maintenance-friendly --preserve-ips=true --airgap=/tmp/airgap-v2.tar.gz
```

deploy-bot: nightly build 2026-03-20T07:40Z: private-distro-v2 pushed.

lisa: Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- upgrades in maintenance-friendly lane must not change external IPs in 3/3 certified customer nets
- median cold-start latency <120ms on baseline hardware
- rollback succeeds and restores previous version in <20min in test harness
- upgrade smoke tests pass (connectivity, KMS, kv-consistency)
- troubleshooting guide present with iptables/ip-forward checks and dual-listen diagnostics
Should we require an "enterprise opt-in SLA" to guarantee no-IP-change?

alex: yes, make `no-ip-change` an enterprise SLA option. If customer opts in we warrant the behavior (and schedule maintenance windows).

customer-noc: We'll draft formal acceptance criteria and share this week. Also: provide a minimal checklist for our NOC on how to validate the install (commands, expected outputs).

sanjay: engineering notes: to avoid IP renumbering for swap-path, we'll need an ip-forwarding shim that binds external IPs and proxies traffic. Estimate 2w infra + 1w QA. Operational cost: increased troubleshooting complexity.

mike: bundle slimming notes: prioritize pruning debug binaries, lazy-download non-critical plugins, and use zstd level 19. If we can split optional modules into on-demand artifacts, base bundle could be ~250-300MB.

alex: action items (owner / due):
- alex: write PRD section describing lanes and SLA option (due Mon)
- mike: run bundle-slim spike and report size estimates (start Mon, 1w)
- lisa: build integration matrix and provision 3 netops sandbox environments for testing (this week)
- sanjay: implement KV/session continuity test harness and rollback automation (due next Wed)
- customer-noc: send formal acceptance criteria + NOC checklist (ASAP)
We'll review at Thu product sync.

mike: include a tiny "how to verify ip preservation" checklist: commands to check `ip addr`, `ss -tnap`, `iptables -t nat -L`, and a curl to the public endpoint that returns a static install-id header.

alex: good. I'll add appendices for troubleshooting and the NOC checklist.

customer-noc: thanks, this aligns well. We'll provide two example firewall rules and our approval matrix by EOW. :thumbsup:
